keyConcerns.headline: Operating reserves are calculated from the FY2022 Form 990, not the FY2024 income statement above

strengths_deep_dive: MedGlobal demonstrates substantial direct service capacity in conflict zones, serving facilities across Gaza, Yemen, and Sudan. Field reports confirm extensive medical interventions, including over <cite id="5">163,000 malnutrition screenings in Gaza</cite> and direct operational support to <cite id="6">67 health facilities</cite>. Financially, the charity maintains a lean fundraising model, requiring <cite id="12">$0.05 to raise every $1 in donations</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: MedGlobal focuses on direct medical relief and emergency healthcare delivery in high-need crisis zones including Gaza, Sudan, Yemen, and Bangladesh. Primary limiting factors affect its evaluation, particularly heavy reliance on non-cash in-kind gifts and governance gaps. Financial filings show <cite id="13">Total Revenue of $33,542,803 in FY2024</cite>, though non-cash gifts represent 94% of reported revenue. While the organization reports an official <cite id="12">70.7% program expense Ratio</cite>, the cash-adjusted program ratio drops to 71%, which falls below the 75% industry standard. The organization maintains an <cite id="12">88/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and demonstrates <cite id="12">a fundraising efficiency of $0.13 per $1 raised</cite>. Operationally, MedGlobal provides direct service delivery, conducting over <cite id="5">163,000 malnutrition screenings</cite> and supporting healthcare facilities in active conflict areas. The organization is <cite id="4">Zakat-eligible</cite>, aligning with Muslim donors seeking to support emergency medical care for vulnerable populations.
